h1: Natural Stone Retaining Walls in London, Ontario
intro: London properties backing onto the Thames River valley or a wooded ravine often call for a wall that looks like it grew out of the landscape rather than one that was built onto it. Natural stone does that.

sections.heading: Where Stone Suits a London Property

blocks.text: Armour stone and boulder walls work particularly well on river valley lots, wooded properties, and anywhere a homeowner wants the retaining structure to read as a natural feature rather than a built one. The irregular shapes and weight of natural stone also make it a strong option for informal terracing.
For a more formal look closer to the house, natural stone can be dry-stacked with tighter joints, still without mortar, relying on the weight and fit of the stones themselves.

sections.heading: How a Stone Wall Is Built

items.title: Base preparation
items.text: Compacted granular base set to depth, sized for the weight of the stone being used.

items.title: Placement
items.text: Larger stones set first as the structural base course, worked with equipment given their weight.

items.title: Batter
items.text: Each course set back slightly from the one below to resist outward soil pressure.

items.title: Drainage
items.text: Drainage stone and filter fabric behind the wall, same as any other retaining system.

sections.heading: Why Drainage Still Matters With Stone

blocks.text: Natural stone's weight and irregular shape help it resist movement, but it still needs drainage behind it in London's clay soil, or water pressure will eventually push it out of alignment.
The City of London requires a permit for walls over roughly one metre, natural stone included. We handle the application and arrange engineering for taller stone walls.

sections.heading: Sourcing Stone for a London Project

blocks.text: Stone availability and size vary by supplier, so we review options with you at the quote stage rather than assuming one stone type. Larger armour stone gives more structural capacity; smaller fieldstone suits garden borders and informal terracing.
For a broader comparison of materials before deciding, /how-to-choose-retaining-wall-material is a useful starting point.

Armour stone is heavy and typically delivered by truck, then placed with equipment. We confirm driveway and yard access during the site visit, since some older London lots have narrower access than newer properties.

faqs.q: Is natural stone as strong as block or concrete?
faqs.a: For lower to mid-height walls, properly built stone performs very well. For very tall or heavily loaded walls, concrete or engineered block is usually the better structural choice.
No, our stone walls are dry-stacked, relying on the weight and interlock of the stones plus proper drainage behind them, similar in principle to interlocking block.

faqs.q: What stone sizes do you use for a London property?
faqs.a: It depends on wall height and the look you want, from smaller fieldstone for garden borders to large armour stone for structural walls.

faqs.q: Can natural stone be combined with plantings?
faqs.a: Yes, the irregular joints and ledges in a natural stone wall work well with trailing plants and garden pockets, more so than a smooth block or concrete face.

faqs.q: Can I choose the specific stone type used in my wall?
faqs.a: Yes, we review available stone options and sizing with you before construction, based on the wall's height and intended look.

faqs.q: Can armour stone be delivered to a narrow older London lot?
faqs.a: Usually yes, though we confirm access during the site visit and may adjust stone size or delivery method for tighter properties.
